data.narrative:
Orbital Inc., a seed-stage space and aerospace company backed by a16z Speedrun, is evaluated against a universe of 5 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including SpaceX, Sierra Space, and Planet Labs.

Standard triangulation methods encounter material constraints. Peer-median analysis is not applicable: while 11 same-sector peers exist, filtering for identical or adjacent stage and valuation tier yields fewer than 3 datapoints, rendering a narrow peer set unreliable. Public-comp anchoring, though theoretically supportable—the Space & Aerospace sector trades at a 23.9x price-to-sales median across the 5 public tickers—cannot be applied because Orbital's revenue is not disclosed, as is typical for private companies at this stage.

The absence of sufficient narrow-peer granularity and revenue disclosure prevents derivation of a supported valuation range through quantitative methods. Any valuation estimate would require either disclosure of Orbital's revenue (enabling public-comp anchoring) or identification of 3+ private peers at identical stage and comparable pre-money valuation tier (enabling peer-median triangulation). Key uncertainties include the company's revenue run rate, customer concentration, and capital efficiency relative to the identified private peer set. Further diligence or data disclosure is necessary to support a robust quantitative range.
